e.etymology: A modern name in the family of Davin, Devin and Daveon.
A modern American combination of Ray or Rae with Anna.
A vintage American elaboration with the -ella ending, built on Love or on the surname Lovell, in the manner of Louella and Luella.
A Scottish and northern English surname meaning son of Jamie, the pet form of James.

assoc.t: Jameson Irish whiskey (spelled without the i)

e.etymology: Used both as a feminine form of Neil and as a spelling of Nayla or Neyla, from the Arabic name Na'ila.
The Irish and Scottish Gaelic form of Margaret, from Greek margarites, pearl. In Irish it is written Mairéad.
e.note: Unfamiliar to many Americans; it rhymes with parade.

e.etymology: A respelling of Aniston, a surname taken up as a girls' name because of actress Jennifer Aniston.
A Japanese girls' name written with various kanji, so the meaning depends on the characters chosen. In English it can also be read as an elaboration of Erin.
A respelling of Kennedy, from the Irish surname O Cinneide, descendant of Cinneidigh, a byname from ceann, head, and eidigh, read as helmeted or as misshapen.
From mesa, Spanish for table and, in the American Southwest, a flat-topped hill with steep sides; also the name of an Arizona city.
A modern American name close to Zora and Zoria, names from the Slavic word for dawn, finished with the -iah ending.
A double-d spelling of Adeline, a French pet form of Adele, from the Germanic element adal, noble.
A spelling of Mireille, a name the poet Frederic Mistral shaped from Provencal mirar, to admire, for the heroine of his 1859 poem Mireio.
A form of Alice used in Welsh and several other languages, from Old French Alis, a shortening of the Germanic name Adalheid, of noble kind.
An English surname. Its recent use as a first name follows Ryle Kincaid, a lead character in Colleen Hoover's novel It Ends with Us and its 2024 film.
e.note: In It Ends with Us, Ryle is the husband who becomes abusive; fans of the book will make the link.

e.etymology: A name used mainly in Mexican American families, more often spelled Karely; it follows the pattern of Arely and Nayeli.
A spelling of Lindy, a pet form of Linda and Lindsay.
From the Japanese word mirai, the future, written with characters meaning not yet come. It is used for both girls and boys in Japan.
A Latin American spelling of Amy, written the way the English name sounds in Spanish. Amy comes from Old French Amee, beloved, from Latin amata.
A modern American coinage joining Ember, a glowing coal, with the -ley ending, on the model of Kimberley.

assoc.t: Tahari, women's clothing label by Elie Tahari

e.etymology: A short form of names such as Zaire, Zaiden and Isaiah, now given on its own.
A modern American coinage joining Gray, the color and surname, with the -len ending of Braylen and Jaylen.
A Yiddish pet form of Yaakov (Jacob), by way of Yankel. Hasidic and other Orthodox Jewish families use it as a given name in its own right.
e.note: Sounds like Yankee to most American ears.

e.etymology: A medieval Danish contraction of Mathias, the equivalent of Matthew, from Hebrew Mattityahu, gift of the Lord.
namesakes: Mads Mikkelsen (Danish actor, Casino Royale and Hannibal)
e.note: In Danish the d is silent, closer to MASS; in the US Mads is also a nickname for Madison and Madeline.

e.etymology: A spelling of Aitana, taken from the Sierra de Aitana, a mountain range in Alicante, Spain. The poet Rafael Alberti gave it to his daughter, and the singer Aitana made it widely popular.
A respelling of Ainhoa, a village in the French Basque Country whose shrine to the Virgin Mary turned the place name into a girls' name across Spain.
A recent name in the pattern of Kalani and Leilani, opening with Sol, the Spanish and Latin word for sun.
A 19th-century short form of Old English names beginning with Ethel-, such as Etheldreda and Ethelinda, from aethel, noble. It was a top American girls' name around 1900.
namesakes: Ethel Mertz (Lucy's neighbor on I Love Lucy)
Ethel Kennedy (wife of Robert F. Kennedy)

assoc.t: Ethel, Lucy's neighbor and sidekick on I Love Lucy

e.etymology: From Germanic ger, spear, and thrud, strength. Saint Gertrude of Nivelles, a 7th-century abbess, spread the name, and it was widely used in America around 1900.

assoc.t: Queen Gertrude, Hamlet's mother in Shakespeare's Hamlet

e.etymology: An English place name and surname from Old English burh, a stronghold, and tun, a farmstead or settlement.
A spelling of Alicia, the Latinized form of Alice, from Old French Alis, a shortening of the Germanic name Adalheid, of noble kind.
